title: Self-Hosted Serving Selection — llama.cpp, Ollama, TGI, vLLM, SGLang

questions.question: Which engine does the lesson pick as the dev-laptop one-command default?
questions.explanation: The lesson positions Ollama as the dev-laptop one-command install for a single user, trading roughly 15-30% throughput versus llama.cpp for ease of setup -- it is not the pick for production scale.

questions.question: What 2025 event changes the default away from TGI for new projects?
options: TGI entered maintenance mode on December 11, 2025 — only bug fixes going forward
questions.explanation: The lesson states Hugging Face TGI entered maintenance mode on December 11, 2025 (bug fixes only), which makes it a risky long-term bet and biases new projects toward vLLM or SGLang instead.

questions.question: Which hardware constraint forces llama.cpp and excludes vLLM / TRT-LLM?
questions.explanation: The lesson's hardware-first decision tree states CPU-only deployments must use llama.cpp (Ollama also works but is slower) since vLLM and TRT-LLM require a GPU accelerator.

questions.question: Which engine does the lesson position for agentic multi-turn and prefix-heavy workloads thanks to RadixAttention?
questions.explanation: The lesson names SGLang as the agentic multi-turn and prefix-heavy specialist, crediting its RadixAttention mechanism and citing 400,000+ GPUs in production at companies like xAI, LinkedIn, and Cursor.

questions.question: What dev-to-prod pipeline does the lesson recommend on the same GGUF or HF weights?
options: Ollama in dev and Ollama in prod
Ollama in dev, llama.cpp in staging, vLLM (or SGLang for prefix-heavy) in prod
questions.explanation: The lesson's 2026 pipeline pattern is dev on Ollama, staging on llama.cpp, and production on vLLM (or SGLang for prefix-heavy workloads), all using the same GGUF or HF weights throughout.

questions.question: Why is Ollama discouraged for shared production?
options: Go HTTP serialization adds overhead, concurrency management is simpler than vLLM, and OpenTelemetry support lags
questions.explanation: The lesson's Ollama caveat is that its Go HTTP serialization adds overhead, its concurrency management is simpler than vLLM's, and its OpenTelemetry support lags -- fine for one user, not for shared production.
